name: Border Glow
description: Move the pointer toward the card's border: from that same side a cone of colored light settles on the edge, a multi-hue mesh rotates around the frame, and a halo shines outside the card.
interactionNotes: The pointer's proximity to the card border and its angle relative to the center create two live CSS variables, and the glow itself happens entirely in CSS — with no continuous render loop. The halo only wakes within the "edge sensitivity" of the border; "animated" gives a one-off four-second sweep. The geometry is not mirrored: angle and proximity are pointer physics and mean the same in RTL.

props.name: edgeSensitivity
props.description: How close the pointer must be to the edge for the glow to wake; 0 to 100. A larger number means you have to come more precisely close to the border.

props.name: glowColor
props.description: Halo color in "H S L" form — such as "40 80 80". If you have a hex, convert it inline to this same form.

props.name: backgroundColor
props.description: Card color. Its lightness sets the light-surface class and the border and shadow harmonize with it.

props.name: glowRadius
props.description: Reach of the halo beyond the card edge, pixels.

props.name: glowIntensity
props.description: Brightness multiplier of the halo; 0.1 to 3.

props.name: coneSpread
props.description: Openness of the light cone on the edge; 5 to 45 percent.

props.name: animated
props.description: On entry, the cone spins a full turn around the card by itself (a one-off ~4-second sweep).

props.name: colors
props.description: The three colors of the edge mesh; they are spread across seven fixed points of the frame so the card border becomes multi-hue.

props.name: fillOpacity
props.description: Strength of the colored mesh fill inside the card near the edges; 0 to 1.

props.name: sweepLoop
props.description: Re-run the entry sweep once it finishes — for non-interactive previews where the card has to stay alive. This option belongs to this component only.

props.name: paused
props.description: Freeze the glow animation without unmounting the card; the current sweep stays where it is.

tips: All the magic is in CSS: JavaScript only writes two variables (`--edge-proximity` and `--cursor-angle`) on pointer move; so the card is cheap and you can place dozens of them side by side.

The halo is visible only on hover or sweep — at complete rest the edge is quietly off, the same default look. If you have a non-interactive card (a list preview or bento), `animated` + `sweepLoop` takes the place of ambient light.
The color mesh is spread across seven fixed points of the frame: your three colors repeat by the map [0,1,2,0,1,2,1] — so with three good hues you see seven different spots.
The default colors are theme-aware: a dark card with a golden glow and a light card with a purple glow (higher intensity and lower fill) — a matching light/dark pair.
Don't set `letter-spacing` on the text inside the card and give Persian text a line height of at least 1.6; the light frame is independent of text direction and needs no mirroring.
